tapeLine: Friday 30 October was the worst session since June: S&P 500 -1.82% to 7,580.07, Nasdaq Composite -2.9%, Dow -572.25 points (-1.1%) to 51,770.31, per AP-based syndications and CBC coverage of the 30 Oct close. For the week the S&P 500 fell 0.57% and the Nasdaq 2.00%. Monday futures levels were not found.
matters:
Intel fell almost 29% on Friday, its worst day since 1974, after a fourth-quarter profit forecast below analyst expectations, per CBC and AP-based coverage (30 Oct). Amazon fell 1.41% to $240.35 after its third-quarter results; coverage cited a weaker profit than expected and $42.4 billion of trailing-twelve-month free cash outflow.

Sources tied the sell-off to renewed doubts over returns on AI spending, following Alphabet’s 12.64% drop on 29 October. The Russell 2000 was up on the week while large tech fell.

For October, the S&P 500 fell about 0.9%, the Nasdaq more than 5% and the Dow gained about 1.7%, per the same reports.

secondOrder: Alphabet, Amazon and Intel were each marked down on spending, cash flow or guidance within two sessions. Coverage linked them to one theme, AI spending returns. That is an observation, not a forecast.

scorecard.text: The prior brief’s read of risk-off in megacap tech held: the Nasdaq Composite fell a further 2.9% on Friday.
The prior brief’s framing of the Alphabet drop as the day’s main event proved too narrow: Friday’s S&P 500 fall (-1.82%) was larger than Thursday’s (-0.3%) and was led by Intel.
Amazon’s reaction, open in the prior brief, resolved: shares fell 1.41% on Friday to $240.35, per 30 Oct reports.
Yield behaviour still cannot be graded: no dated, sourced yield levels were found.
